lines.text: hands, of the delusive supposition that we ourselves can find
the way which leads to the fulfilment of our life and to our
true self; resignation of the fancy that we ourselves are
powerful, are the masters in control of things. To have the
"light of life" means to have no further question to ask. Do
we wish that? Are we willing to give up our questioning
attitude, our persistent "why and wherefore"? For so long
as we ask, we are anxious to be the masters of ourselves.
Yes, we often wish for each other light in the darkness of
our days and in the mystery of our destiny. But we shall only
receive it when we pray for light to illuminate the darkness
of our inner being. Discipleship implies the confession that
here in our inmost being the darkness is thickest, it implies
the readiness to receive our true selves as a gift from the
hands of God, and to allow ourselves to be re-created as
children oflight in the light which streams from the Holy Child.
But if we are so prepared, God wills to bestow His gift on
us. To such preparedness the Christmas hymn of Novalis
applies:
"See the far glory in the kindling east!
The time comes round that makes the old world new.
Rise-let us drink triumphant at the feast
Of light itself, diffused in every hue!
The powers on high have read man's deep desire
And Love transformed comes down in heavenly fire."
He bestows upon us the "light of life", that unquestioning
transparent luminosity of our being. For in Him the love of
God shines fully; because, if we are so prepared, He becomes
understandable to us as the very act and initiative of the
divine love, as the gift to us of the divine love. It is the love
of God which has always sustained us and ever will sustain
us. To be sustained and held by the love of God means to
have an attitude of unquestioning childlike acceptance, to be
